title: A recursive core for partition function form games
abstract: We present a well-defined generalisation of the core to coalitional games with externalities, where the value of a deviation is given by an endogenous response, the solution (if nonempty: the core) of the residual game.
summary_en: When coalitions form in cooperative games with externalities (a coalition's payoff depends on what other coalitions form), the standard 'core' concept becomes unstable. Kóczy proposes a 'recursive core' that resolves the conceptual problem: each candidate coalition structure is evaluated by considering what the residual non-members would do recursively. The paper shows the recursive core is well-defined and exists under broad conditions, providing a workable solution concept for cooperative bargaining where the value of cooperation depends on what others do.
data_used: Theoretical model — partition-function-form games with externalities. No primary dataset.
policy_relevance: Direct relevance for analysing international climate agreements (Kyoto, Paris), trade-bloc formation (EU, USMCA), and energy-market coalitions (OPEC) where externalities between coalitions are central. The recursive-core concept gives a rigorous tool for evaluating which coalition structures will form when the costs/benefits of forming a coalition depend on what rivals do.
